The Secret Agent Denim is a 14oz Japanese denim developed from a fabric that was nearly discarded. During development in Japan, an entire lot of denim was unintentionally water damaged, and the indigo developed unevenly across the surface.
Rather than allowing the fabric to go to waste, the mill collaborated with a nearby Japanese dye house to carefully bleach the denim at the fabric stage. In our very early Wythe development, we knew we wanted to have a core bedford cord program - we had found so many vintage garments worn by cattlemen and ranchers in the 40s and 50s and the fabric spoke to us in a way that just felt right. These vintage pants were so broken in, so soft, yet still managed to feel bulletproof. We loved how it broke in and knew this was going to be a staple of ours. And while the five-pocket pattern from Wythe has gone through many different stages of fit and fabrication, we've now settled on a level of consistency across our different fabrics that we're very happy with.
This particular bedford cord is just what we were looking for in a workwear staple. It's woven on vintage selvedge loom by a Japanese mill that specializes in weaving this fabric, exactly like it used to be made in the 40s and 50s. It's one of the only fabrics this mill produces.
One of the amazing things about bedford cord is how hard wearing it is on the outside, but how soft and stretchy it is on the inside. It breaks in and molds to your body like raw denim, and is easy to see why this was a favored fabric for workwear.

Our zippered work jacket, made from 14oz broken twill selvedge denim. Broken twill denim was first used in 1964 by Wrangler as a solution for combatting fabric twist caused by the directional torque generated in the weaving process. The process of weaving fabric in this method sees the combination of both right hand twill (RHT) and left hand twill (LHT) reversed every two warp ends, forming a zigzag-like pattern in the denim and resulting in no bias in either direction of the weave.
